inputs.base_revenue_note: PRO FORMA continuing FY2026, not the statutory figure: reported continuing revenue 2,189.0 less the single quarter of QMS consolidated (77.4) plus QMS full-year pro forma revenue 295.4 (FY2026 AR note 6.1, line 7719-7720). Domain, Radio, Pedestrian excluded; NBN/Darwin as affiliates.
inputs.share_count_basis: fully diluted: 1,585.762m issued ordinary shares at 30 June 2026 plus 10.019m performance rights (FY2026 AR EPS note dilution line). Held FLAT because SBC is expensed in the flows; no unissued shares or options at the report date and no current buy-back.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 AR statement of changes in equity, share-based payment expense net of tax (line 5500): 2,400 thousand. No equity-award tax withholding line; rights are settled in shares or cash at the Board's election.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in AUD: 10-year Commonwealth bond ~4.4% plus a 5.5-6.0% Australian equity risk premium at beta ~1.15 gives a cost of equity of ~11%; bank debt at ~6.3% pre-tax (4.4% after 30% tax); bank net debt is ~33% of enterprise value at the valuation date. Blended ~8.8%, rounded to 9.0%. The same 9.0% is used in all three scenarios: structural-decline and leverage risk is carried in the flows and the weights, not in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment B, leases as operating cost. The QMS acquisition took lease liabilities from 333.2 to 919.4 (633.4 acquired), so reported post-AASB 16 EBITDA is heavily flattered: Outdoor shows a ~70% EBITDA margin. The full cash lease payment (principal plus interest) is charged inside EBITDA via lease_cost_pct_path, lease liabilities of 919.4 are EXCLUDED from net debt, and da_pct_path is D&A excluding right-of-use depreciation. FY0 lease cash is an ESTIMATE of ~148 (6.1% of pro forma revenue): ~48 for continuing Nine ex-QMS, ~100 for a full year of QMS. The QMS figure is not disclosed directly; it is backed out of the company's own net leverage of 1.7x (net debt 658.0 over EBITDA less cash lease payments implies a denominator of ~387 against pro forma EBITDA of ~516) and cross-checked against lease interest plus right-of-use depreciation on the acquired liability.
inputs.nci_treatment: Immaterial after the Domain sale: non-controlling interest in equity is 0.8 and the FY2026 NCI profit share is -0.7. No deduction made.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route, with the non-US adaptations (AUD WACC, lease treatment B, SBC near zero). Nine is an operating media company (free-to-air TV and 9Now, Stan, publishing mastheads, and from 31 March 2026 QMS outdoor), so the dcf-methods routing table sends it to the operating-company row; no memory entry existed, this is the first valuation. BASIS: the forward build is PRO FORMA CONTINUING OPERATIONS with a full year of QMS, not an extrapolation of the consolidated history. FY2026 statutory net income of 511.3 includes an 849 after-tax discontinued-operations result (Domain gain 670) and a 481 post-tax specific-item charge (mostly non-cash Total TV impairment, licences 419.2); neither is in the flows. FY2026 reported FCF of 35.6 (OCF 162.2 less capex 126.6) is NOT a usable base: it is levered (47.2 interest paid), contains one quarter of QMS, part-year discontinued operations and restructuring cash, and is before 45.2 of lease principal. last_fcf follows the house identity (35.6 - 2.4 SBC - 0 interest income = 33.2) for auditability only; the valuation is driven by the component paths. Capital gains tax on Domain (169.5) was paid in FY2026 inside investing, so no tax liability is carried in the bridge. DEBT: 750.4 of bank facilities at 30 June 2026 after the QMS draw-down (the 0.7 at 31 December 2025 was a post-Domain trough and is not used). The 3.0c final dividend (47.6) was paid on 22 October 2026, after the balance sheet date and before the valuation date, and is deducted in the equity bridge. BUYBACKS: none since FY2024 (67.5); the flat count is a modelling convention funded by the small SBC charge. Interest income not stripped: the company is in net debt. GUIDANCE (FY2026 results, 26 August 2026, via the Analysis JSON; no numeric group EBITDA guidance): ~60% of revenue and ~70% of EBITDA from Streaming, Digital Publishing and Outdoor in FY2027; Total TV costs broadly flat in FY2027; Outdoor EBITDA up double digits; publishing licensing revenue held at FY2026 levels; cumulative cost-out above 160 over the three years to FY2027 (105 removed in FY2026); dividend payout 60-80% of NPATA. The year-1 margin in each scenario is built from these by segment.

equity_bridge.item: FY2026 final dividend paid 22 October 2026 (3.0c per share)
equity_bridge.note: FY2026 AR, significant events after balance date, line 4069-4070: 47,572,864. Cash left after the 30 June balance sheet; the price is ex-dividend.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: segment build on the pro forma continuing portfolio (historical CAGRs are not usable, see notes)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-8.2% 5yr) diverges by more than 30% from EPS CAGR (+26.2% 5yr). Neither is a growth signal: equity fell because 912 of dividends (777 special) were distributed in FY2026 and Total TV was impaired, while FY2026 EPS of 0.32 is inflated by the Domain gain.
historical_growth.notes: All CAGRs are computed on the reported consolidated series FY2021/FY2023 to FY2026 and straddle the Domain, Radio and Pedestrian disposals and the QMS acquisition, so they describe a different company from the one being valued. FCF CAGRs use owner FCF (reported FCF less SBC; no interest strip, the company is in net debt): 286.4 (FY2021), 248.2 (FY2023), 33.2 (FY2026). On the company's own continuing basis FY2026 revenue grew 3% and EBITDA 17% including one quarter of QMS. The equity-CAGR default is not applied; the base growth path is built by segment: Total TV declining ~4% a year, Stan growing 10% fading to 4%, Publishing ~1%, Outdoor 8% fading to 4%.

base.ebitda_margin_note: Post-AASB 16 EBITDA before specific items, the company's own measure. FY0 pro forma is ~21.4% (378.8 reported less 54.5 QMS quarter plus 191.9 QMS full-year pro forma = 516.2 on 2,407). Year 1 is built by segment from the FY2027 guidance: Total TV costs broadly flat, so a ~4% revenue decline falls straight through (TV EBITDA ~134 to ~94); Outdoor EBITDA up double digits (~192 to ~215); Stan ~81 to ~95; Publishing ~150 with licensing held at FY2026 levels; corporate ~-41. That sums to ~513 on ~2,453, about 21.0%, slightly BELOW the pro forma base. The margin then rises ~0.3pp a year on mix as Outdoor and Stan outgrow TV. Net of the lease charge it is ~14.6% in year 1 and ~15.2% in year 10: the growth is in lease-heavy Outdoor and brings its site rents with it.
base.da_pct_note: Excludes right-of-use depreciation (leases are charged in lease_cost_pct_path). Continuing FY2026 D&A of 150.3 includes ~82 of right-of-use depreciation group-wide.
base.capex_pct_note: FY2026 capex 126.6 (PPE 31.5, intangibles 95.1) plus a full year of QMS digital-screen capex puts FY0 near 6% of pro forma revenue; eased to 5.0% as the technology-platform consolidation completes, held above D&A.
base.cash_tax_rate_note: Australian statutory 30%. FY2026 underlying effective rate was 27.3% (53.4 on 195.8); no loss shelter assumed.
base.wc_capture_note: Advertising-funded with a modest subscription book; program-rights cash is assumed to track amortisation. No working-capital tailwind taken.

scenario_narratives.base: Total Television keeps shrinking at about 4% a year as linear audiences migrate (the metro TV ad market fell 9.6% in FY2026; Nine held a 42.8% share and was down 2% excluding the Olympics). Management guides Total TV costs broadly flat in FY2027, so the revenue decline drops through to earnings in year 1 and later cost-out only slows the erosion. Stan compounds from 569 of revenue at 10% fading to 4% on sport and the new ad tier, without the bulk of NRL streaming rights, which went to Foxtel in the July 2026 renewal; Publishing holds, with digital subscription growth (+15% in FY2026) offsetting print and licensing flat as guided; QMS delivers the guided double-digit EBITDA growth in FY2027 and grows revenue 8% fading to 4% with the ~20 of cited cost synergies. Group revenue grows 1-2% and the post-AASB 16 EBITDA margin moves from ~21.0% in year 1 to ~22.7% on mix, but because the growth is in lease-heavy Outdoor the margin after site rents only edges from ~14.6% to ~15.2%. Terminal value is capped at 12x for a business whose largest revenue line is in structural decline; the cap binds.
scenario_narratives.bull: The portfolio restructure works as management describes it: the 'Sofa to Street' cross-platform proposition wins share, Total TV declines only ~1.5% a year as 9Now monetisation offsets linear, Stan sustains double-digit growth with advertising on Stan Sport and Stan Entertainment and margin expanding toward the high teens, QMS grows near 10% with revenue synergies on top of the cost synergies, and AI content-licensing deals (Microsoft Copilot, the News Bargaining Incentive) add high-margin publishing revenue. Group revenue grows 2.5-4.5% and the margin after leases rises from ~16.7% to ~18.3%. It needs TV stabilisation, Stan scale and a clean QMS integration to all hold, which is why it carries a 25% weight rather than the house 35%.
scenario_narratives.bear: The free-to-air advertising decline does not moderate: Total TV revenue falls ~8% a year against a cost base loaded with fixed sports rights (roughly 145-150 a year for NRL free-to-air through 2034), and cost-out cannot keep pace once the easy savings are taken. Stan growth slows to mid-single digits against global streamers and Foxtel's NRL streaming position, print decline overwhelms digital subscriptions in Publishing, and QMS, bought for 850 while outdoor was the fastest-growing ad segment, grows only ~3% while its long-dated site leases stay fixed. Group revenue shrinks for five years, the margin after leases falls from ~12.9% to ~10.8%, and with 658 of bank debt (1.7x on the company's own lease-adjusted measure) almost all of the enterprise value belongs to lenders. The dividend would not be covered on this path.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the house 15/50/35 to 25/50/25. Bear raised to 25%: the largest segment by revenue is in structural decline (and was impaired by ~480 post tax in FY2026), and the group has just levered to 1.7x to buy a lease-heavy cyclical asset, so equity value is highly sensitive to the downside path. Base 50%: it extends the FY2026 continuing-operations trends and the stated cost-out program. Bull cut to 25%: it needs several independent things to go right at once (TV stabilisation, Stan scale, QMS revenue synergies).

valuation_philosophy.summary: Nine is valued as the continuing portfolio it now is (Total TV, Stan, Publishing, QMS Outdoor), on pro forma FY2026 economics with a full year of QMS, with site and property leases charged as an operating cost so that Outdoor's post-AASB 16 margin does not flatter the flows. The equity is a levered residual on a business where one large segment shrinks while three smaller ones grow; the valuation therefore turns on the pace of Total TV decline and on whether QMS earns its 850 purchase price, and the scenario spread is wide for that reason.
key_risks_to_valuation: The lease charge is an estimate: QMS cash lease payments (~100 a year assumed) are backed out of the company's 1.7x net leverage disclosure, not read from a full-year cash flow statement. Each 10 of annual lease cost is worth roughly 0.04-0.05 per share in the base case.

The base year is pro forma, built from a note 6.1 disclosure and one consolidated quarter of QMS; the first full-year result (FY2027) will be the first clean check on revenue, margin, capex and lease cash.
Pace of free-to-air advertising decline: Total TV is still ~43% of pro forma revenue and each percentage point of annual decline compounds through the margin via operating leverage.
Leverage: 658 of bank net debt plus the October 2026 dividend against ~150 of unlevered owner FCF; the bear case leaves little for equity.
QMS acquisition accounting is provisional (12-month window) and 459 of goodwill sits on the Outdoor segment.
Sports and content rights renewals (Stan Sport, Olympics, NRL, tennis) can reset the cost base in steps the smooth margin path does not capture.

No numeric FY2027 group earnings guidance exists; the year-1 margin is a segment build from qualitative guidance (TV costs flat, Outdoor EBITDA up double digits) and no post-August trading update was available in the filings on hand.
